items.headline: Google threatens to cut school districts' Search access over AI
items.summary: Google issued an ultimatum to school districts to accept AI summaries in Search or lose access on school accounts, prompting pushback from Chicago, Los Angeles, and New York City. The nation's largest districts now face choosing between softening AI restrictions or finding another search engine.

items.headline: Cybersecurity expert warns rogue humans, not AI, are the threat
items.summary: Former NSA hacker David Kennedy described how 30+ AI agents overwhelmed a company's network defenses in 14 minutes, stealing data and demanding ransom. The analysis argues AI gives hackers superpowers, but human actors remain the real cyberthreat.

items.headline: Enterprises push ahead with AI despite no federal regulation
items.summary: Corporate tech leaders say state laws in California, Colorado, New York, and Texas are now the operating standard after midterms settled the question of federal AI oversight. Executives warn a patchwork of state rules could hurt companies but won't stop innovation.

items.headline: Anthropic shares begin trading on Nasdaq in record IPO
items.summary: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on November 19 after pricing its IPO at $83 a share, raising $81.3 billion plus a $26 billion private placement for a total haul of $107 billion. The debut topped SpaceX's record raise and could pave the way for an OpenAI IPO next year.

items.headline: Anthropic lays out four ways it wants to disrupt science
items.summary: Coinciding with its IPO, Anthropic detailed ambitions to cure diseases, accelerate discovery, and automate science, including its acquisition of an AI-powered biotech. Many researchers remain skeptical of the company's lofty claims about transforming drug discovery.

items.headline: Anthropic commits to $44.9 billion Microsoft Azure spend
items.summary: Anthropic modified its agreement with Microsoft, committing to spend at least $44.9 billion with the company between November 2026 and May 2033. The deal deepens Anthropic's cloud ties as it brings Claude models to Azure ahead of its IPO.

items.headline: Anthropic details Fable 5.2 circuit board design gains
items.summary: Anthropic demonstrated that Claude Fable 5.2 scored 69% on an internal PCB Gym benchmark versus 25% for Fable 5, and 83.5% on the public BenchCAD 2.1 test. The results show sharp improvements in AI capabilities for electronics and hardware engineering tasks.

items.headline: Can the AI boom make enough money to sustain itself?
items.summary: The Economist examines whether surging AI revenue can justify the massive capital buildout as Wall Street grows concerned about how companies are funding the boom. The analysis highlights uncertainty over AI timelines and the hazy exercise of valuing AI-driven stocks.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
items.summary: Anthropic launched two new frontier models, its first since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow the pace of AI development in September. The company said the models underwent rigorous safety testing and that it 'called for pacing, not pausing.'
